category_title: Students using informal visuospatial representations for arithmetical reasoning
minimal_context: The student is working on completing a requested grouping of a 2D dot array.
dialogue:
TUTOR: Here is the 2D dot array. Please complete the requested grouping of the dots.

STUDENT: I'm going to use a counting-based strategy. One, two, three... I'll draw a circle around these. This is what I perceive to be most efficient for me right now.

TUTOR: What do you think you should do next?

STUDENT: (Finishes drawing circles) I made an array-container blend. Now I want to spontaneously work through all the different possible equal groupings.

TUTOR: Okay, go ahead.

STUDENT: (Erases the page and starts counting every single dot from the beginning again) I'm choosing a very long-winded strategy to find the next groups. Attempting to retrieve number facts doesn't work for me, so I just have to count them all one by one again to make it meaningful.

options.A: Ignore the student's behavior aimed at getting attention and reinforce positive behaviors based on extinction and differential reinforcement principles.
options.B: Provide visual expectations or rules and a visual chart with the time on it for the dot array grouping activity.
options.C: Allow the student to decide that the task is not over yet and extend the grouping activity in a way that intrigues them.
options.D: Stop the student's action and provide an explanation that not all of the dots in the array have been grouped.
